entry.title: Fix what the review found, all three in the note 📝
entry.content:
Fix what the review found, all three in the note 📝

Two of them lose typing, and both were in the seam between a box that is
being typed into and a sync that is not waiting for it.

push() and corePull() read the local store before opening their GET and
merged against that snapshot, so anything typed while the round trip was
open was written straight back out — one keystroke at a time, with the
loss PATCHed to the gist behind it. They read after the round trip now,
which is also right for a page turned mid-pull.

paintR() skips a focused box so a pull cannot take a half-typed sentence
away, but nothing repainted it afterwards: a note merged in while the box
sat focused and empty was overwritten by the next keystroke. focusout
repaints, which is what the comment already claimed.

The third is a test rather than the product. 読み込み on a hidden box only
opens and clears it, so the two-click idiom parsed an empty string and
import-merges-rather-than-replaces passed without ever importing. The box
is revealed explicitly now, in the manage suite and in the review suite
that copied the idiom.

Both new assertions fail against the pre-fix engine and pass after.
156 assertions pass.

entry.title: Let the reader say what a story was worth ⭐
entry.content:
Let the reader say what a story was worth ⭐

Five stars and a 感想 box on every row of the contents page, neither
behind 編集 — a rating is given on the way out of a story, not sat down
to. Tapping the lit star takes it back off, which is the only undo there
is. reviews.py is the reading end: it joins the ratings to the level,
register and length each was a verdict on and prints the notes in full,
and AUTHORING.md now runs it at Gate 1.

Reviews are a second map in the same gist rather than fields on the
progress record. A progress record is replaced whole by whichever side
carries the later timestamp and every page turn bumps it, so a rating
stored there would be erased the next time another device turned a page
in the same story.

Also fixes a latent race the new suite surfaced: two edits inside one
millisecond carried the same `at`, the merge gives a tie to the remote,
and the second edit then lost to the copy of the first its own push had
already put in the gist — a stepper tap that silently undid itself.
Edit stamps on the contents page are now monotonic; the merge rule still
gives the remote a genuine tie so two devices converge. Frozen-clock
assertion, which fails against the old code with page 25 for 24.

152 assertions pass, 728 with --matrix.

entry.title: Sync reading progress to a secret gist, and make it correctable
entry.content:
Sync reading progress to a secret gist, and make it correctable

localStorage loses reading progress three ways, and only one of them is
"two devices disagree": WebKit deletes all script-writable storage after
seven days of browser use without a visit, and a Home Screen web app
starts with a storage container of its own. A secret gist answers all
three, with no server, no open port and no account that wasn't already
open.

New scripts/sync.js is the store, the merge rule and a GitHub gist
client, shared by every reader and by the contents page. The reader
pulls on open and pushes on the existing Store.defer flush, so a
reading session costs one or two gist revisions rather than forty. A
device connects by pasting a token and nothing else -- the gist is found
by filename, so no gist id is ever carried between devices.

The contents page gains an edit mode: mark a story read or unread, move
the resume page, clear one story, export and import the whole record as
JSON, and a link to the gist itself. Import merges by the same rule the
sync does, so pasting a stale export cannot pull a story backwards.

Two rules the manage UI forced, both about what can travel:

- done set by reading is sticky and OR'd, but an OR cannot carry an
  un-mark -- it restores it from whichever device was not told. A hand
  correction writes doneAt, and the later doneAt then decides outright
  in both directions.
- A deletion cannot travel either, since an absent slug merges back to
  whatever the gist still holds. Clearing writes a dated, page-less
  tombstone instead.

Two permanent-failure bugs found while writing the tests: connect()
awaited the queued pull() it was itself holding, deadlocking the one
path every new device takes; and a persisted ETag with a cold in-memory
cache earned a 304 meaning "unchanged from nothing", which the ETag then
survived, so the device would never have synced again.

Also adds a web manifest and icons. Installing to the Home Screen is
what actually stops the seven-day purge, because a standalone web app
has its own counter of days of use -- but it starts empty, so connect
the token first or the install reads as data loss.

docs/versions/ stays frozen and is now also sync-free: sync.js is
written only by write_engine, never by the inline render() path, so an
archived draft never pushes a slug only one device has a story for.

698 harness assertions pass, matrix included, across new sync and manage
suites driven by a fake gist API. Seven deliberate breaks of the new
code are each caught by a named assertion. All seven data/<slug>.js are
byte-identical and docs/versions/ is untouched.

Not yet exercised against a live token. 📖

entry.title: Add 行かなかった人の地図, a level 5 folktale quest
entry.content:
Add 行かなかった人の地図, a level 5 folktale quest

The longest story in the corpus at 48 pages, and the first with a
supernatural element. A dying man asks his granddaughter to walk the
road he spent fifty years drawing and never once travelled. Every
landmark is wrong, because the map records his father's journey
rather than the land, and a told journey does not update.

grammar_focus is にとって, chosen because the construction and the
theme are the same thing: one object meaning something different to
each person who holds it. It lands on seven separate pages.

folktale register carries the magic for free. The 主 on the 峠 costs
nothing from the new word budget, since 主, 姿, 影, 声, 問う and 通す
are all already known.

Misses its page brief: 48 against 40, +20 percent. Recorded in the
corpus entry rather than corrected. The brief was the thing that was
wrong, picked off the requested range before the beat sheet existed.

All other targets met. repeated_share 72.7 percent is the highest in
the corpus; all 8 new words clear the 8 occurrence minimum.

entry.title: Fix what the review found, starting with the one that mattered 🔍
entry.content:
Fix what the review found, starting with the one that mattered 🔍

.w:hover was beating .w.lit. Both are (0,2,0) and the hover rule is the
later one, so the light rendered at the hover tint — and the pointer is
still on the word at the moment it is clicked, which meant a desktop
single click produced no visible change at all until the cursor left.
The light is the only feedback that gesture has. :not(.lit) on the hover
rule, with a comment saying why it is load-bearing.

lastAt = 0 was not a safe "sequence restart" sentinel. performance.now()
is milliseconds since page load, so for the first 300ms of a session it
still reads as "just now" and a third fast tap would re-enter the double
branch instead of toggling off. Clear the node instead.

Two harness rows could not fail, which is the worse kind of green:

  light-drops-when-its-node-is-recycled asserted "#track .lit" finds
  nothing after removing the lit node — but a detached node is not inside
  #track whether the observer ran or not. Assert on the clone itself.

  a-tap-in-the-reserve-summons-the-bars ran straight after reset(), which
  goes through Track.goTo, which calls Chrome.show() unconditionally. The
  bars were already up before the tap. Hide them first and assert the
  precondition alongside the result.

Both were mutation-tested: with the observer's light(null) and Track's
Chrome.show() each disabled in turn, both rows now fail.

And the reserve strip is documented. It is the only way left to summon
the bars now that every tap on the text means something, and neither the
key legend nor the README mentioned it. README also claimed Tab reaches
every sentence; it reaches translated ones, because the others have
nothing to open.

665 assertions green with --matrix.

entry.title: Let the tap say what the buttons used to 👆
entry.content:
Let the tap say what the buttons used to 👆

One tap on a kanji word lights its reading in place. Two inside 300ms open
the sheet with the gloss. A tap on the kana and punctuation between words
does the same for the whole sentence, and its double tap gives the English.

That is the whole of what the bar's three gate buttons were for, so they
go: the reading and the meaning stay one gesture apart rather than one
button apart, and the page finally does something before anything is armed.

build.py only wraps a kanji-bearing token in a .w, so particles, kana words
and punctuation were already bare text inside the .s. Non-word is about half
of every line, which is why the sentence gesture needed no markup at all.

The detector keys on the resolved .w/.s inside Sheet rather than on the raw
pointerdown target in Track: a word's first tap can land on its ruby and the
second on the kanji beside it, and comparing d.down would miss about half of
all real double taps. Node identity also makes a recycled cell read as the
fresh first tap it is. The first tap is not deferred, because lighting is
additive and moves no layout, and the window is tested before the unlight
branch so a fast repeat can never flicker off and on.

lit and the panel come apart: the light outlives the sheet, which is what
lets one tap mean "reading" on its own. Two fields and one invariant replace
the lit/subject/sticky triad, enforced in light() alone.

Gone with the gates: the trans and meaning prefs, their settings switches,
the t/m keys, the 意 hint, the desktop hover preview, and the rule that kept
the bars up while a gate was armed. Sheet reads no prefs now. Full-page
ふりがな survives, in 設 and on f. Tab reaches every word and sentence and
Enter opens the sheet, which is the keyboard's double tap.

Two things to judge on the device. The bars are harder to summon now that
every tap on text is consumed: what falls through is the cell's chrome
reserves, the 16px gutters and the unfilled part of the page box, which is
comfortable in 横書き and about 120-150px of an 844px phone in 縦書き
flowing. And a fat-fingered miss now lights a sentence rather than doing
nothing; if that reads as too eager the fix is a nearestWord() tried before
the sentence.

665 assertions green with --matrix, four of them new.

entry.title: Rebuild docs/ into the linked form 📚
entry.content:
Rebuild docs/ into the linked form 📚

The first build through render_linked. Six shells at ~5KB apiece where
there were six documents of 200-280KB, one reader.css and one reader.js,
and six data/<slug>.js carrying what used to be inlined six times over.
18,500 lines out of the published tree.

The corpus did not move. Checked key by key against HEAD~2's inline DATA
on all six: pages, sentences, tokens and every 苦手 / 新出 / unknown
marking identical. One field differs, in all six and by the same amount —
knownVocab 6502 → 6504, two cards matured past the 21-day interval since
the last build. vocab.py reads ankimorphs.db live, so that number moves
on its own schedule and has no mtime anywhere for staleness to notice.

docs/versions/ is untouched, which is now the steady state rather than an
omission: the five archived drafts keep the engine they published with.

661 assertions pass against these readers, with --matrix.

Still unverified on real iOS Safari, which is the target. Two things in
particular want eyes on the phone rather than the emulator, because
headless Chrome has no safe-area insets and so shows neither:

- The header saving only pays where there is a notch to pay it. Screen
  counts are unchanged at an emulated 390x844 and should drop on the
  device, where the reclaimed 22px crosses a character boundary.
- Centring short screens shifts the text block by up to half a column
  between turns, and most screens are partial by design.

entry.title: Give the story back the space the chrome was borrowing 📖
entry.content:
Give the story back the space the chrome was borrowing 📖

Ten fixes off the first sustained read on the phone, in 縦書き 改行-off,
which is the shipped default and the configuration none of this had been
looked at in.

The reported "space before every new sentence" is the 全角 paragraph
indent, not a per-sentence gap. blockPlan groups narration runs correctly
— page 1 of 迷子の手紙 is six sentences in three <p> — so the indent was
firing twice on that screen, on the two narration paragraph openings, and
reading as a defect because a column that starts a character low next to
one that does not is what the eye actually sees. It is redundant in 縦書き
anyway: a <p> is a block, so a paragraph already opens a new column and
the column break IS the separation. That is the argument the stylesheet
already made for 改行-on. Scoped to 横書き, where it is the only marker.

The bar scrims were veiling live text. Both gradients were drawn at
top: 100% / bottom: 100% — outside the bar and over the page box — while
.cell pads by --top-h and --bar-h and never by --scrim. Roughly 20px off
the head and foot of every column, permanently, whenever the chrome was
up. Removed. If an edge is ever wanted back it has to be paid for out of
the page box rather than borrowed from it.

横書き leading 2.6 → 2. The 1.94em floor derived for 縦書き is geometry,
not a fact about vertical text: rotate the page and ruby is still 0.44em
on one side of the line and 傍点 0.5em on the other. 2.6 was spending an
extra line of leading every four lines to buy nothing.

目次 moves into the button bar, so the top bar carries no tap target and
is sized to its own text: --top-h 114px → 92px on a phone with a notch,
which is one more character per column. Two things that risked, both now
asserted, both found by measuring rather than by reading the diff:

- Seven 44px targets overflowed a 320pt bar by 10px, and the symptom is
  次 half off the screen edge. The elastic 目次 padding and narrower bar
  gutters fit it. An eighth control would look fine in the source.
- The title sat 4.8px left of centre. Its start padding has to carry the
  flex gap as well as the count's width; the gap sits between title and
  count and nowhere else.

Tapping an open word closes it, with no timing window, which is the
double-tap that was asked for and more forgiving than one on a phone —
a second tap thirty seconds later works too. A dblclick listener would
have been fighting the track, which owns pointer capture and suppresses
the synthesised click. Gated on sticky, or the first real click on a
word the mouse had merely passed over would close a sheet nobody opened.

Chrome ships hidden. Stamped in init rather than by calling hide(), whose
armed-gate refusal is right for an auto-hide mid-read and wrong at boot,
where a gate left armed in a previous session would put the bars up.

Short screens centre in the box (align-content). Extent is capped so a
median authored page fills about 70%, so most screens are partial and one
that is very short was hanging off the block-start edge — in vertical-rl
that is the right, and a one-sentence screen read as right-aligned
against empty paper. The cost is a shift of up to half a column between
turns. .page.tight still overrides back to start.

The disclosure sheet drops into the bar's space when the bars fade,
instead of floating a bar's height above empty paper. The page box
reserves --bar-h either way, so it covers less text, never more.

Reflow on chrome-hide was considered and rejected. The page box being one
constant rectangle is what makes the fade safe; a box that grew on hide
would repaginate mid-read, which is the failure PageBox.suspend() already
exists to prevent during a drag — and chrome hides on a drag.

661 assertions pass, --matrix included.

entry.title: Link the engine instead of inlining it into every reader 🔗
entry.content:
Link the engine instead of inlining it into every reader 🔗

A one-line CSS change rewrote 2.5MB and needed Ichiran and a live Anki to
do it. rebuild.py globbed reader.* into the staleness set for every story,
so touching reader.css marked all eleven readers stale, and each rebuild
re-segmented the whole story to produce a DATA blob identical to the one
already on disk. Self-containment was the right shape while a story was a
file to mail; it stopped being worth that once the site was published.

docs/ becomes one reader.css and one reader.js beside a ~5KB shell per
story and its own data/<slug>.js. Classic <link> and <script src> only —
fetch() and type="module" are both blocked on file://, and classic scripts
run in document order, which is what guarantees window.STORY exists before
the engine reads it. A story still opens off the filesystem; it needs its
siblings now, so it is a folder to copy rather than a file to mail.

Three outputs with three dependency sets, which is the whole point:

  data/<slug>.js   the story .txt, the afterword, the .py engine
  <slug>.html      reader.html, build.py
  reader.css/.js   reader.css, reader.js, build.py

Only the first needs Ichiran and Anki. Editing the reader now rewrites two
files in about a second with Anki closed, and re-segments nothing.

render_split was already most of this and was labelled "not a shipping
format"; it is now the same code path the live tree uses, with flat
filenames for a one-story scratch directory. The __STORY_DATA__ →
window.STORY substitution lives once, in build.write_engine, which
rebuild.py imports rather than re-implementing — 01ffd51's lesson.

docs/versions/ is frozen rather than merely self-contained. Archived
drafts leave the default rebuild loop entirely and keep the engine they
published with, because an archive that re-renders with today's code
preserves the story and not the reading it shipped with. --versions
rebuilds them anyway. This is a change in what the archive means: an
engine fix will not reach an old draft. That is the intent and the cost.

stats.read() now answers from either form, because both exist: data_of
tries the inline blob first and falls back to the sidecar, so index.py and
the harness do not have to know which shape a given reader took.

Checked before the rebuild that follows:

- A shell-only regeneration (touch reader.html) reproduces the full
  build byte for byte, with no segmentation pass.
- An engine-only change (touch reader.css) reports every story up to
  date and writes only the two assets.
- check_contracts now asserts the script order in the linked shell. It
  is invisible in the markup and would fail every story at boot with
  DATA undefined; the fixtures are rendered inline, so nothing else here
  would have caught it.

docs/ is unchanged in this commit; rebuild.py has not run.

entry.title: Make the harness assert the build rather than imitate it 🔬
entry.content:
Make the harness assert the build rather than imitate it 🔬

The module docstring says the page under test is byte-for-byte what
build.py emits. It was not: build() re-implemented render()'s three
substitutions and stats.ROW's regex rather than calling them, so a fourth
placeholder added to reader.html would ship in every reader and in none
of these fixtures, and the suite would quietly measure a page build.py
never produces. That is the exact failure the harness was written to
prevent, reintroduced one level up.

scripts/ was already importable — SRC is computed on line 45 — so the
contract assertions stay (a marker that stopped matching exactly once is
still a hard error, checked once per run in check_contracts) and
build.render() does the substituting. The local function is now
build_fixture, since `build` is the module.

Two things the suite could not have caught, because of how it ended:

tapAt(bareSpot(s)) passed a possibly-null point. The rescan loop above it
can finish without assigning, leaving `s` on a node the track has already
recycled — Prefs.setAll between the two re-splits every screen — and
bareSpot then returns null. tapAt(null) dereferenced pt.x, the promise
rejected, br.eval raised, and main()'s finally closed the browser with
suite_marks, suite_persistence and suite_degradation never run. Every
other fixture gap in this file returns a failed row; these three now do
too, and the sentence is re-resolved against the live screen at each tap
instead of carried across a re-split.

apply_prefs wrote three fields. Prefs persist across navigations on one
origin, so suite_persistence's dark theme, left binding, 36px and three
armed gates leaked forward into everything after it — and
suite_degradation runs with storage throwing, so it could not overwrite
them either. With --matrix that meant all 288 cells ran at binding left
with 訳 and 意 armed, while the cell label claimed only
viewport/mode/density/size. Chrome.hide() refuses to hide with a gate
armed, so that path was dead for the whole matrix, and the right-bound
turn direction — the 縦書き default, half the matrix — was never
exercised at any point in the suite's life. Every field is written now.

Also here:

- A new gesture case, drag-is-continuous-through-its-origin, which
  reports jump: 14 against the pre-fix engine and under 1px after it.
- The fixture directory is removed on the way out. It was created at
  import and never cleaned, unlike Chrome's profile, leaving ~1.7MB in
  /var/folders per run and one run per --table or --matrix invocation
  during a tuning session.
- serve() takes directory= rather than issuing a bare os.chdir, which
  moved the whole interpreter's working directory — and build.py and
  stats.py are imported here and resolve paths of their own.

657 passed, 0 failed, with --matrix.

entry.title: Let each fact be stated by whatever already knows it 🔑
entry.content:
Let each fact be stated by whatever already knows it 🔑

Three things the reader was re-deriving, each from something that only
looked like evidence.

読了. index.py decided a story was finished with `page >= total`, while
the reader's own rule also requires the last authored page's LAST screen
(reader.js Progress.mark). On shuden that page splits in two at 28px on a
390x844 phone, so turning to screen 1 of page 23 painted the bar to 100%,
printed 読了 and counted it in the 読了 N/M header with a screen still to
go. The record already carried `done`; the contents page ignored it and
re-derived the verdict from a convention written down in two places. It
now reads the field, and Progress is the only thing that decides it.

The 目次 link. A version build was identified by a dot in DATA.slug.
build.py knows the story stem and rebuild.py chooses the output depth, so
both knew this was a nested build and the reader had to infer it from a
filename convention — which broke on both sides: a story slug carrying a
dot would link out of docs/ entirely, and renaming the archive form from
slug.v1 to slug-v1 would point every version build at a sibling
index.html that does not exist. rebuild.py now passes --toc and build.py
writes it into DATA.

A full quota. Store.writeJSON treated every write exception as "this
store is permanently unavailable", which is right for Safari private
browsing and wrong for QuotaExceededError. Twelve readers share one
origin and one progress map that is never pruned, so one story filling it
would have stopped the type size, the writing mode and the theme
persisting as well, silently, for the rest of the session. Firefox names
it NS_ERROR_DOM_QUOTA_REACHED, so the name is matched rather than the
code.

Also here, all in reader.js:

- `reduced.addEventListener` ran unguarded at module-evaluation time
  inside the Track IIFE. Chrome.bind guards the identical call for
  prefers-color-scheme; on an engine whose MediaQueryList predates
  addEventListener this one throws before the bootstrap runs at all, and
  the symptom is a blank page on a target the README names by hand
  (mailed, or dropped onto a tablet).
- The live drag offset was discontinuous at dx === 0. `dx - Math.sign(dx)
  * TAP_SLOP` is only correct on the half-line the gesture started on, so
  dragging a live swipe back through its own start point moved the page
  16px in one frame and flipped which neighbour was being revealed. The
  slop is now fixed at the moment the gesture goes live.
- Every interrupted snap leaked its transitionend listener. settle()
  clears the transition before resetting the transform, which cancels it
  — and cancellation fires transitioncancel, so the listener never ran
  and never removed itself. A held arrow key registered one per key
  repeat and dropped them all on the next snap that actually landed.
- Ten exported members and two returned fields no call site ever read,
  shipped inline in all twelve HTML files: Progress.clear, Prefs.reset,
  Prefs.V/FONT_MIN/FONT_MAX, Store.disable, Track.invalidate/paint/busy/
  setMouseDrag, PageBox.clearMeasure, Paginator.screenCounts, and
  Progress.open's `restored` and `done`.

And four comments citing line numbers that had moved or a file that is
not in the repository: README:21 and AUTHORING.md:109 in reader.css,
plan:67 in reader.js and plan:78 in harness.py. Cited by section and by
assertion name instead.

Verified: 657 harness assertions pass. The 読了 change is checked in
headless Chrome against six seeded progress records, two of which fail
against the previous index.py; the drag change has a new harness case
that reports jump: 14 — exactly 2 * TAP_SLOP — against the previous
engine.

Nothing here reaches docs/ until rebuild.py runs.

entry.title: Correct the documentation the rewrite falsified 📝
entry.content:
Correct the documentation the rewrite falsified 📝

README.md and the instructions index.py prints on the contents page both
taught hover-for-the-reading, click-to-pin, 訳-reveals-every-translation and
click-a-line-for-one-translation. All four are now false, and the contents
page is where every reader lands.

Rewritten for what the reader actually does: tap a word for its reading in
the sheet, 意 adds the meaning, 訳 arms translations and then a sentence tap
shows its own, ふ reveals every reading, swipe or the arrows turn pages, 設
holds the settings. The two disclosure gates are described as separate,
because that separation is the point of the tool.

Also corrects the marking description — 傍点 replaced the underlines — and
notes that text is vertical by default, that a page never scrolls, and that
preferences and reading position persist.

And the footer, which has listed five stories since 煙突の煙 was added.

entry.title: Show per-story progress on the contents page 📊
entry.content:
Show per-story progress on the contents page 📊

The readers now record where you stopped. This surfaces it.

Progress cannot be baked in at build time — it lives in the reader's
localStorage on the device, not in the repo. So index.py emits a script that
reads japanese-stories:progress at runtime and decorates each row. Pages
serves the contents page and every reader from one origin, so the store the
readers write is the store this reads.

Each row carries data-slug and data-pages, and card() now computes the slug
once and hands it to version_links(), so a row's identity and its version
hrefs cannot disagree.

The page index stored is the AUTHORED one, never a screen index, so progress
survives a change of type size, density or device — which is the reason the
authored page had to stay the atom.

Defensive by default: the whole thing is wrapped, since a mailed or file://
copy throws on the accessor itself. A record that is not an object is skipped
rather than trusted, so a version field added at the top level later cannot be
read as a slug. rec.of is ignored in favour of the row's own count, because it
is only what that device believed last time. A page past the end clamps.

Verified in headless Chrome against seeded storage: a mid-story record renders
its bar and count, a done record and an over-the-end record both read 読了, a
story with no record stays hidden, a string-valued record and an unknown slug
are both ignored, and the header tallies 読了 2/6. The .prog[hidden] rule is
mandatory and asserted — display:flex would otherwise beat the UA rule and
show an empty bar on every unread story.

entry.title: Add the verification harness 🔬
entry.content:
Add the verification harness 🔬

656 assertions over four mode x density cells, three viewports and
22/28/36/40px, plus behaviour, 傍点 geometry, persistence and degradation
suites. Drives Chrome over CDP with a hand-rolled websocket, since nothing
is installable here.

The harness this replaces was circular and that is why it shipped three
blockers. It asked PageBox.overflows() on every live screen — the same
predicate split() used to choose the boundary — so "0 overflowing" across
162 pages was true by construction and could not fail. It also injected a
style block pinning the track to an explicit box, replacing the layout root
it was meant to be testing.

This one asserts raw geometry against the live cell: scrollWidth against
clientWidth, the bounding rect contained in its parent, documentElement
scroll unchanged from baseline. A tight run is a failure, not a counter. It
drives device metrics through CDP so the page is byte-for-byte what build.py
emits, and holds one browser open across navigations so reload, cross-story
and before-and-after checks are reachable.

It also asserts build.py's four substitution contracts on every run, so a
marker that stopped matching exactly once fails loudly rather than silently
shipping a broken reader.

Lives in tools/ rather than scripts/, because rebuild.py globs scripts/*.py
into DEPS and a harness there would mark every story stale on each run.
